positively to benzodiazepines. 2 recently, several patients have been described whose symptoms were strictly conﬁned to 1 lower limb. this condition was ﬁven the name ‘ ‘stiff-limb syndrome’ ’ (sls). 3 generally considered to be a focal form of sps, sls usually has a poorer response to benzodiazepines. anti-gad antibodies are less common in sls than in sps: 15% vs. 88%, respectively. 3 comprehensive treat- ment recommendations are not available, as clinical tri- als are hampered by the rarity of the syndrome. 3 we report the case of a 40-year-old woman who pre- sented with a 9-year knee-extension spasms were superimposed on submaximal extension stiffness with emotional stimuli. repeated magnetic reso- nance imaging of the entire spinal cord and the brain were normal. routine laboratory tests were unremark- able, apart from mildly elevated glucose levels. immuno- logical parameters were also negative. four years after the onset of symptoms she was tested for anti-gad anti-
